locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (Hydrogen rearrangement to a saturated heteroatom with adjacent cleavage)

evidence.curator_note: Same six-membered H-rearrangement as eq 4.37 (the lower 'rH' arrow of the shared scheme on p.76), reproduced here as the first step of the charge-migration channel eq 4.38. The alcohol is n-ionized at oxygen (O+. localized, convention B); the delta C-H (map 3) is abstracted by the oxygen radical. ARC COUNT: the book draws 3 arc(s) and all three fishhooks are printed -- move <1> = O odd electron (map 7) into the forming O7-H8 bond; move <2> = one C3-H8 sigma electron into that O-H bond; move <3> = the other C3-H8 electron onto carbon map 3. Product = the distonic ion with a carbon radical (map 3) and a -O+H2 oxonium (map 6-O7). Instantiated for 1-hexanol (M = C6H14O, m/z 102), whose C2H5 terminus is drawn explicitly in this branch.

locator.section: 4 / Basic Mechanisms of Ion Fragmentation (charge migration, inductive cleavage 'i')

evidence.curator_note: Charge-migration ('i', inductive) water loss of eq 4.38: the C6-O bond of the oxonium ionizes heterolytically, both bonding electrons going to oxygen so that neutral HOH departs and the charge migrates onto carbon map 6 (a carbenium ion); the carbon radical on map 3 is untouched, giving the distonic hydrocarbon radical cation C6H12+. at m/z 84 (11%). ARC COUNT: the book draws 1 arc -- a single full (double-barbed) arrow from the C6-O7 bond onto the oxygen (drawn as the arc looping off 'HOH+'), so no implicit hook is needed; move <1> carries electron_count 2. (The arrow checker reports a soft note that the +2 electrons landing on oxygen form a lone pair rather than two radicals -- expected for a heterolytic cleavage.)

Cross-linked to MOD rules IMS_4_38_rH and IMS_4_38_ind; VERIFIED against their DFS. IMS_4_38_rH (identical DFS to IMS_4_37_rH) '[C]1[C]2[C]3([H]4)[C]5[C]6[C]7[O+.]8[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]5[C]6[C]7[O+]8([H]4)[H]9' = step_rH_hydrogen_rearrangement (H4 = my map 8 migrates C3 -> O8, my map 7). IMS_4_38_ind '[C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C]6[O+]7([H]8)[H]9 >> [C]1[C]2[C.]3[C]4[C]5[C+]6.[O]7([H]8)[H]9' breaks C6-O7, makes C6 a carbenium ([C+]6), releases neutral water ([O]7) and leaves the C3 radical intact -- exactly step_i_inductive_water_loss_charge_migration. A fourth rule, hTransition_saturated_2 (src/data_generation/rules/IMS_bookCover.py), is also filed under eq 4.38 in the index but its DFS '[H]1[C]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C.]6 >> [C.]2[C]3([_A+]4)[C]5[C]6([H]1)' describes a CARBON radical (map6) abstracting an H from a carbon (map2) with a generic charged substituent [_A+] as a spectator -- NOT the oxygen-radical-driven rH drawn on p.76 -- so it does not match this scheme's H-transfer (listed in rule_mismatches).
